summary: ~32% of corpus chunks (994/3089, v27) are retrievable but are apparatus/boilerplate, not content: site nav ('Sacred Texts... Previous Next'), tables of contents ('Next: Chapter IV', 'Next: Book XI'), and editorial/manuscript footnotes ('the word aidum stood... in his MS'). Found via the tuning experiment (59060e24): LLM-judged precision@10 is ~0.2 corpus-wide and ~0.00 for distinctive small-tradition queries because the surfaced chunks are this junk (Zoroastrian Gathas results are philological footnotes, not doctrine). This — not ranking weights (which moved precision <0.06) — is the dominant retrieval-precision lever. FIX IS UPSTREAM in the guru pipeline chunker: filter/strip apparatus at ingestion + re-export. Cross-repo. Evidence: docs/concept-hierarchy/tuning-experiment.md Round 2.
